# Normal Models and Nuisance Parameters

- [A mean with known variance](#a-mean-with-known-variance)
- [A mean with unknown variance](#a-mean-with-unknown-variance)

## A mean with known variance

- Conjugate normal updating; precision and shrinkage
- Prediction for a future observation versus inference for a mean

Agresti 3.1

## A mean with unknown variance

- Joint, marginal, and conditional posterior distributions
- Conjugate normal–inverse-gamma structure and Student t marginals
- Semi-conjugate independent mean/variance priors as a later Gibbs example

Agresti 3.2 and 3.4

# Multiple Parameters and Large Samples

- [Comparing and combining means](#comparing-and-combining-means)
- [Conjugacy and large-sample approximations](#conjugacy-and-large-sample-approximations)

## Comparing and combining means

- Two-group differences and several-group comparisons
- Multivariate normal structure as a bridge to linear models

Agresti 3.5–3.6; selected supplementary multivariate material

## Conjugacy and large-sample approximations

- Exponential families, Poisson–gamma updating, and asymptotic Bayes/ML behavior
- Local normal and Laplace approximations; boundaries, skewness, and multiple modes

Agresti 3.7; supplementary approximation notes

# Exact and Computational Answers

- [Monte Carlo as an integration tool](#monte-carlo-as-an-integration-tool)
- [Planned Python demonstration](#planned-python-demonstration)

## Monte Carlo as an integration tool

- Approximate posterior summaries with directly generated draws
- A short sampler/diagnostics primer if software requires MCMC

Agresti 3.3; formal treatment in Posterior Computation

## Planned Python demonstration

- Check simulated normal-model summaries against exact results
- Separate posterior uncertainty, approximation error, and Monte Carlo error

No companion notebook released yet
